title: pvVisItPixieReader
body:
## pvVisItPixieReader

Reads 2-D and 3-D HDF5 output of the Pixie3D extended-MHD code: rectilinear or curvilinear grids with node- and cell-centred fields over the stored time steps. ParaView 5.13.3 has no native Pixie reader. One file supplies every time step the format stores.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Many codes write .h5 files; make sure the file is Pixie3D output before choosing this reader.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrays and CellArrays: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- The VisIt plugin's own read options stay at their defaults; the ParaView proxy exposes no property to change them.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItPixieReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItPixieReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrays` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from Pixie3D data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The Pixie3D plugin offers the node- and cell-centred fields of the HDF5 file; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | Path of the single Pixie3D file to read (.h5); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Materials` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The Pixie3D plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Meshes` | Names of the Pixie3D meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The Pixie plugin reports rectilinear or curvilinear meshes depending on the run, and point meshes for particles. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrays` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from Pixie3D data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The Pixie3D plugin offers the node- and cell-centred fields of the HDF5 file; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItPixieReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
